parsed.justification: All standard policy sections are present (purpose, scope, roles, principles, requirements, exceptions, monitoring, references) with technically sound controls aligned to NIST SP 800-63B (length over complexity, no forced expiry, modern hashing) and NATO references. Minor weaknesses: A.5.17 is cited as ISO/IEC 27002 (it is the 27001/27002 access info control, generally OK) but '8.2.3' and 'A.10.1' citations don't map cleanly to ISO/IEC 27001:2022/27002:2022, and the principle of 'no periodic expiry' for users coexists with admin 180-day rotation without contradiction but the 'three character classes' fallback slightly conflicts with the modern NIST stance — minor inaccuracies rather than contradictions.
evidence_quotes: No periodic (time-based) expiry for user accounts unless compromise is suspected or system risk assessment dictates.
MFA (smartcard + PIN/password) is mandatory for all NS, MISSION SECRET, and privileged accounts.
All passwords must be stored using salted, strong, cryptographic hashing (e.g., bcrypt, PBKDF2, Argon2).

parsed.justification: The policy is heavily tailored to this specific NATO multinational detachment in Romania: it references the four classification domains (NU/NR/NS/MISSION SECRET), ISSM/J6 chain, SOFA, host-nation Romanian CSL, NATO-specific directives (C-M(2002)49, AC/322-D(2017)0009, AC/35-D/1029, AJP-3.20), NCIRC processes, and the 25 FTE security staff and 40 hours/year training figures from the context. Operational constraints like classification spillage, two-person integrity for break-glass, and host-nation liaison are visibly woven throughout rather than generic boilerplate.
evidence_quotes: applies to all personnel (military, NATO civilian, and cleared contractors) who access, administer, or manage CIS assets, applications, and networks at all classification levels (NU, NR, NS, MISSION SECRET)
Host-Nation Liaison Officer | Coordination of cross-jurisdictional compliance (GDPR, Romanian CSL), escalation of legal issues
Password sharing is strictly prohibited except for emergency break-glass accounts (with auditable two-person integrity).

parsed.justification: Citations are pervasive and tied to nearly every control, referencing real, identifiable artefacts (NIST SP 800-63B, ISO/IEC 27002:2022, NATO C-M(2002)49, AC/322-D(2017)0009, GDPR Art. 25). However, some citations are imprecise or questionable: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 uses control numbers like 5.17, 8.5, 8.16, not '8.3.3/8.3.4/8.3.5' (those resemble the older 27002:2013 numbering), and 'ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.10.1' / 'A.6.5' do not map cleanly to the 2022 Annex A. These inaccuracies prevent a 5, but the citation discipline is otherwise strong and not fabricated wholesale.
evidence_quotes: (Ref: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.10.1, NATO INFOSEC)

parsed.justification: All controls fit comfortably within the stated resource envelope: 25 security FTE, theatre 24/7 SOC, existing PKI/smartcards, and well-funded budget make MFA, hashing, lockout, and monitoring requirements clearly implementable. Operational constraints (classification separation, two-person integrity for break-glass, COMSEC) are explicitly respected, and exception/compensating-control mechanisms are provided.
evidence_quotes: MFA (smartcard + PIN/password) is mandatory for all NS, MISSION SECRET, and privileged accounts.
Password sharing is strictly prohibited except for emergency break-glass accounts (with auditable two-person integrity).
Exceptions may only be granted in writing by the ISSM, following risk assessment, and must be time-bound with compensating controls.

parsed.justification: The policy systematically references the major applicable frameworks (NATO C-M(2002)49, AC/322-D(2017)0009, AC/35-D/1015/1029, AJP-3.20, GDPR, Romanian CSL/NIS2, SOFA, NIST CSF/800-63B/800-53, ISO/IEC 27001/27002) and ties controls to specific clauses. However, conflicts/overlaps between regimes (e.g., GDPR vs NATO classification handling, host-nation reach vs SOFA limits) are only implicitly acknowledged via a liaison role rather than substantively addressed, and CTS-level handling is not mentioned.
evidence_quotes: Romanian Cybersecurity Law (Law 58/2019; NIS/NIS2)
Host-Nation Liaison Officer | Coordination of cross-jurisdictional compliance (GDPR, Romanian CSL), escalation of legal issues
Privacy by Design: User credential data must be protected in accordance with GDPR and host-nation law. (Ref: GDPR Art. 25, Romanian CSL)

parsed.justification: Nearly every substantive control carries an inline attribution to specific clauses (e.g., NIST SP 800-63B §5.1.1.2, ISO/IEC 27002:2022 8.3.3, AC/322-D(2017)0009 §20), distinguishing between frameworks rather than lumping. However, some references remain section-level or generic (e.g., 'NATO INFOSEC', 'C-M(2002)49' without clause, 'NATO IRP/NCIRC SOP'), preventing a full audit-ready 5.
evidence_quotes: All user passwords: ≥14 characters *(Ref: NIST SP 800-63B §5.1.1.2, ISO/IEC 27002:2022 8.3.3, AC/322-D(2017)0009 §20)*
MFA (smartcard + PIN/password) is mandatory for all NS, MISSION SECRET, and privileged accounts. *(Ref: AC/322-D(2017)0009 §21, NIST CSF PR.AC-7, ISO/IEC 27002:2022 8.4.2)*
Administrative/privileged accounts: 180-day maximum validity, or upon change of assignee. *(Ref: NIST SP 800-53 IA-5, NATO INFOSEC)*

parsed.justification: The policy makes only incidental references to resource elements (25 FTE security staff, 40 hours/staff/year training) without using them to justify control choices, phasing, or trade-offs. There is no explicit calibration of ambition to the budget/staff envelope; controls are stated as absolutes with no acknowledgement of constraints or staged implementation.
evidence_quotes: Security Staff (25 FTE) | Monitoring, auditing, incident response, user awareness training, policy enforcement
Training and awareness outcomes will be assessed as part of the annual training cycle (minimum 40 hours/staff/year).
